mainTopic: How a tree on the border of an עיר מקלט is treated, a killer or לוי who kills inside a city of refuge, and honoring a killer in exile
overview: The amud opens with רבי יהודה, who says a cave goes by its entrance and a tree goes by its boughs. The גמרא pushes back: he may have meant this only as a stringency for מעשר שני. For ערי מקלט, following the boughs could let the גואל הדם kill a man standing inside the city. רבא answers that everyone agrees a man at the trunk inside is safe, and a man in boughs outside who can be shot is not. The real argument is whether the trunk may be climbed as a step to reach him. רב אשי answers differently: 'follow the boughs' means 'follow the boughs too.' A new משנה teaches that a killer who kills again inside his city of refuge moves to another neighborhood, and a לוי moves to another city. A ברייתא shows that exile already existed in the desert, to the camp of the לויים. The amud ends with a משנה: a killer offered honor must first say 'I am a killer,' and if they still insist, he may accept.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a tree follows its boughs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יהודה's view, 'follow the entrance of a cave, follow the boughs of a tree,' as the source for the ברייתא that follows the boughs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: with a cave, go by its entrance; with a tree, go by its boughs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה to show whose opinion the ברייתא follows. The ברייתא said that for a tree on the border, we go by its boughs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a cave, what counts is where its opening is. For a tree, what counts is where its branches hang, not where its trunk stands. That fits the ברייתא, so the ברייתא seems to follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Its boughs, the branches and top of the tree

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
With regard to a cave, follow its entrance;
with regard to a tree, follow its boughs.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בִּמְעָרָה הַלֵּךְ אַחַר פִּתְחָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the search, from before this section, for whose view the ברייתא follows.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא that says to follow the boughs for both מעשר שני and ערי מקלט
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's ruling: with a tree, follow its boughs

steps.title: רבי יהודה may have meant only a stringency for tithes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהודה followed the boughs only for מעשר שני, because there it makes things stricter in both directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say that you only heard רבי יהודה say this about tithes, as a stringency. If the trunk is outside and the boughs inside, just as you may not redeem under the boughs, you also may not redeem at the trunk. If the trunk is inside and the boughs outside, just as you may not eat without redeeming under the boughs, you also may not eat without redeeming at the trunk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to reject the proof from רבי יהודה. It suggests his rule might only be a חומרא that applies to מעשר שני, and it sets up the contrast with ערי מקלט in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מעשר שני, treating the trunk like the boughs only adds restrictions. If the boughs are inside, you may not redeem at the trunk, as if you were inside. If the boughs are outside, you may not eat unredeemed at the trunk, as if you were outside. Either way it is a stringency, so it does not prove that רבי יהודה treats the boughs as the real rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, or perhaps; it introduces a pushback against a proof
Here, מעשר שני: produce that must be eaten in ירושלים or redeemed outside it
To redeem, redemption (exchanging the produce for money)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying the trunk is truly treated like the boughs. In both cases here we treat the spot as both inside and outside, whichever is stricter.

phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Yehuda say this
with regard to tithe, as a stringency:
its trunk is outside and its boughs are inside,
phrases.notes: Outside or inside the wall of ירושלים.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דִּבְנוֹפוֹ לָא מָצֵי פָּרֵיק –
phrases.english: just as among its boughs one cannot redeem,
so too at its trunk one cannot redeem.
Its trunk is inside and its boughs are outside,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דִּבְנוֹפוֹ לָא מָצֵי אָכֵיל בְּלֹא פְּדִיָּיה –
phrases.english: just as among its boughs one cannot eat without redemption,

phrases.aramaic: בְּעִיקָּרוֹ נָמֵי לָא מָצֵי אָכֵיל בְּלֹא פְּדִיָּיה.
phrases.english: so too at its trunk one cannot eat without redemption.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה גַּבֵּי מַעֲשֵׂר לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the proof from רבי יהודה by limiting his rule to a stringency for tithes.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits רבי יהודה's 'follow the boughs' to מעשר שני, where it only adds restrictions
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A rule that is used only as a חומרא cannot be stretched into a general rule that also gives leniencies.

steps.title: For cities of refuge, following the boughs would let him be killed inside
steps.stepSummary: For ערי מקלט, a trunk outside with boughs inside works fine. But a trunk inside with boughs outside would mean the killer could be killed while standing inside the city, which is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with cities of refuge: granted, if the trunk is outside and the boughs inside, then just as he cannot be killed in the boughs, he also cannot be killed at the trunk. But if the trunk is inside and the boughs outside, would we say that just as he can be killed in the boughs, he can also be killed at the trunk? He is standing inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why רבי יהודה's tithe rule cannot carry over to ערי מקלט. In one of the cases, it would lead to an impossible result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ערי מקלט, following the boughs is not always strict. When the trunk is inside and the boughs are outside, it would let the גואל הדם kill the רוצח at the trunk, even though he is inside the city. Since that cannot be, the ברייתא, which follows the boughs for ערי מקלט, seems not to fit רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Cities of refuge, where an accidental killer (רוצח בשוגג) is protected
Granted; it accepts one case before challenging another
Kill (here, the גואל הדם killing the רוצח)

phrases.english: But with regard to cities of refuge,
granted, if its trunk is outside and its boughs are inside,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דִּבְנוֹפוֹ לָא מָצֵי קָטֵיל לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: just as among its boughs he cannot kill him,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the גואל הדם, and 'him' is the accidental killer.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעִיקָּרוֹ נָמֵי לָא מָצֵי קָטֵיל לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: so too at its trunk he cannot kill him.
But if its trunk is inside and its boughs are outside,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דִּבְנוֹפוֹ מָצֵי קָטֵיל לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: would we say that just as among its boughs he can kill him,
at its trunk he can also kill him?!
But he is standing inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the pushback by showing the tithe stringency cannot work for ערי מקלט.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא, which follows the boughs for ערי מקלט, matches רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Following the boughs when the trunk is inside would allow killing a man who is standing inside the עיר מקלט, which is absurd.

steps.title: רבא: two cases where everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that some cases are not in dispute. At the trunk inside the city, no one may kill him. In the boughs outside, where he can be reached with arrows and stones, everyone agrees he may be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: at the trunk, everyone agrees that he cannot kill him. If he is standing in the boughs, and he can kill him with arrows and pebbles, everyone agrees that he can kill him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins to answer the challenge. He removes the impossible case from the argument by saying everyone agrees on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says רבי יהודה never meant that a man at a trunk inside the city may be killed. Everyone agrees he is safe there. Everyone also agrees that a man up in boughs outside the city, who can be hit with arrows or stones, is not protected. So the real argument must be about some other case, which רבא will go on to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees; there is no argument here

steps.whyThisMatters: By taking these cases out of the argument, רבא saves the link between the ברייתא and רבי יהודה and narrows down what the מחלוקת is really about.

phrases.english: Rava said:
At its trunk, everyone agrees
that he cannot kill.
If he is standing among its boughs,
and he is able to kill him with arrows and pebbles,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּמָצֵי קָטֵיל לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: everyone agrees that he can kill him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּעִיקָּרוֹ דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by setting aside the impossible case as one everyone agrees on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the dispute to other cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following the boughs would let the גואל הדם kill a man at a trunk inside the city.
steps.terutzMaskana: At the trunk inside, everyone agrees he is safe. In the boughs outside, within reach of arrows, everyone agrees he may be killed. The dispute must be about something else.

steps.title: The real dispute: can the trunk be used as a step to reach the boughs?
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his answer. רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue only about whether the trunk inside the city may serve as a step to reach a killer on the boughs outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they do disagree is whether the trunk can be a step for the boughs. One Sage holds that it can, and the other holds that it cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer from Step 4. He now pinpoints the one case where רבי יהודה and the רבנן really disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The killer sits on the boughs that stretch outside the city, and the גואל הדם can only reach him by climbing the trunk, which stands inside the city. רבי יהודה says the trunk may be used as a ladder, so the killer is unprotected. The רבנן say climbing the trunk inside the city to get at him is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: its trunk (the base of the tree)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shrinks the argument down to one narrow case. The rule that nobody may be killed while inside the city stays fully in place.

phrases.english: Where they do disagree
is whether its trunk becomes a step for its boughs.
phrases.notes: Picture the גואל הדם climbing the trunk, which is inside the city, to reach the killer out on the branches.

phrases.english: One Sage holds:
its trunk does become a step for its boughs.
And the other Sage holds:
its trunk does not become a step for its boughs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by naming the exact point of dispute after listing the cases everyone agrees on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the dispute to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's 'follow the boughs' seemed to mean a killer could be killed while standing inside the city.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is only about whether the trunk may be climbed to reach the boughs outside. Inside the city he is always protected.

steps.title: רב אשי: 'follow the boughs' means 'follow the boughs too'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer. רבי יהודה did not mean to look only at the boughs. He meant to add the boughs alongside the trunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What does 'follow the boughs' mean? It means follow the boughs as well.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second way to answer the problem from Step 3. He rereads רבי יהודה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem only came up because 'follow the boughs' sounded like 'ignore the trunk.' רב אשי says the word means 'also.' The trunk keeps its status and the boughs are added to it, so the impossible case of a killer being killed inside the city never comes up.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבא and רב אשי. רבא keeps the plain meaning and narrows the argument. רב אשי changes how we read the words themselves.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
What does 'follow the boughs' mean?
Follow the boughs as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מַאי אַחַר הַנּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רבא's to the same challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the words of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Follow the boughs' means only the boughs decide, even against the trunk.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Follow the boughs' means the boughs are added to the trunk. The trunk is never ignored.

steps.title: A killer who kills again inside the city of refuge, and a לוי who kills
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. A killer who kills again inside his city of refuge moves to a different neighborhood in that city. A לוי who kills moves to a different city.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he killed in that same city, he is exiled from one neighborhood to another. A לוי is exiled from one city to another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה. It deals with someone who kills by accident while he is already living in a city of refuge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A killer already in exile has nowhere better to run, so he simply moves to another neighborhood in the same city. A לוי already lives in a city of refuge as his home, so for him, exile means moving to a different city of refuge.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he killed in that same city,
he is exiled from one neighborhood to another,
and a Levite
phrases.notes: The cities of refuge were Levite cities, so a לוי already lives in one.

phrases.english: is exiled from one city to another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the tree discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A killer who kills inside his city of refuge moves to another neighborhood. A לוי who kills moves to another city.

steps.title: A ברייתא: exile already existed in the desert
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק 'and I will appoint for you a place.' It shows that refuge existed in משה's lifetime and that Israel exiled killers even in the desert.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'And I will appoint for you a place, etc.' 'For you' means in your lifetime. 'A place' means from your place. 'Where he may flee' teaches that Israel exiled killers in the desert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא connected to the משנה's rule about a לוי. It reads the פסוק word by word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'For you' teaches that refuge began during משה's own life, before entering the land. 'From your place' points to משה's own camp, the camp of לוי. 'Where he may flee' teaches that killers were really sent into exile in the desert.

keyTerms.meaning: and I will appoint for you a place (the פסוק being read)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
'And I will appoint for you a place, etc.'
'And I will appoint for you' means in your lifetime.
'A place' means from your place;
phrases.notes: משה was a לוי, so 'your place' points to the Levite camp, as the end of the ברייתא shows.

phrases.english: 'where he may flee'
teaches that Israel would send killers into exile in the desert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא linked to the משנה's rule about a לוי and the Levite places of refuge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Exile for accidental killers already applied in the desert, during משה's lifetime.

steps.title: Where did they go in the desert? The Levite camp
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks where killers were sent in the desert. It answers that they went to the camp of the לויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: To where did they send them? To the Levite camp.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a clarifying question and answers it right away. In the desert, the place of refuge was the Levite camp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were no cities in the desert, so the camp of the לויים did the job the cities of refuge would later do. This fits the משנה, which ties refuge to the לויים.
steps.whatToRemember: Refuge was always linked to the לויים: first the Levite camp in the desert, later the Levite cities in the land.

phrases.english: To where did they send them?
To the Levite camp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact location of the desert exile mentioned in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where were killers exiled to in the desert?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To the camp of the לויים.

steps.title: A לוי who kills is exiled from district to district
steps.stepSummary: From the desert law, the חכמים learn that a לוי who kills goes to a different district. If he went to his own district, it still protects him.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: a לוי who killed is exiled from one district to another. And if he was exiled to his own district, his own district protects him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא draws a practical rule from what it just said about killers in the desert. It tells us where a לוי who kills must go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the desert, killers were sent to the camp of the לויים (step 9). So a לוי, who already lives in a city of refuge, cannot be exiled by simply staying home. He must move to another district. But if he did end up in a refuge city in his own district, that place still protects him.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said: a rule learned from what came just before
A לוי, from the tribe that lived in the cities of refuge
Protects him and takes him in as a refuge

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a different case from step 7. It explains the משנה's 'from city to city': a לוי who kills moves to a Levite city in another district. The new point is that if he went to a city in his own district, it still protects him.

phrases.english: From here they said:
A Levite who killed
is exiled from district to district,
and if he was exiled to his own district,
his district takes him in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical rule for a לוי from step 9's answer that killers in the desert went to the camp of the לויים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לוי who kills is exiled to a different district, but if he went to a refuge city in his own district, it protects him.

steps.title: The פסוק that a killer's own city of refuge still protects him
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא brings the פסוק 'for in his city of refuge he shall dwell.' It means a city that already took him in can keep protecting him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא said: What is the פסוק for this? 'For in his city of refuge he shall dwell.' That means a city that already took him in.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא asks which פסוק teaches the rule, and then answers with a פסוק that calls it 'his' city of refuge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'his' (מקלטו) shows the city already belongs to him as a refuge. So even after something new happens, like killing again inside it, he does not lose its protection. He just moves within it, which matches the rule of the משנה in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק? A request for the source in the תורה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the exact word in the פסוק that teaches a refuge city keeps protecting a killer it has already taken in.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa son of Rav Ika said:
What is the verse?
"For in his city of refuge he shall dwell"
a city that has already taken him in.
phrases.notes: The key word is 'his'. It is already his refuge, so it keeps protecting him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא: מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the rule that a city that already took the killer in keeps protecting him.
steps.raayaObject: A city of refuge that already took in a killer keeps protecting him; he moves within it rather than leaving.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 35:28, 'כי בעיר מקלטו ישב', where 'his' city means one that already took him in.

steps.title: A killer whom the city wants to honor
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if the people of the refuge city want to honor a killer, he must first tell them he is a killer. If they still want to, he may accept.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, a killer who was exiled to his city of refuge, and the people of the city wanted to honor him, should say to them, 'I am a killer.' If they say to him, 'Even so,' he may accept it from them, as it says: 'And this is the matter of the killer.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives a rule about honor. A killer living in a city of refuge must tell people what he is before accepting honor from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The killer may not hide his status to get honor. But he only has to say it once, 'I am a killer.' If they still want to honor him, he may accept. The פסוק uses the word 'דבר', which hints at speaking: he must 'say' it.

keyTerms.meaning: Similarly, a case like the one before
Killer, here meaning someone who killed by accident
To honor him, for example by giving him a position
The matter of the killer; 'דבר' hints that he must speak up

steps.whatToRemember: A killer in exile must say 'I am a killer' before accepting honor. If the people still want to honor him, he may accept.
steps.confusionAlert: He is not forbidden to accept honor. He only has to tell them the truth first.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Similarly,
a killer who was exiled to his city of refuge
and the people of the city wanted to honor him,
he should say to them, "I am a killer."
If they said to him, "Even so,"
he may accept it from them,
as it says: "And this is the matter of the killer."
phrases.notes: דברים 19:4. The word דבר sounds like 'speak', so he must say that he is a killer.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ, רוֹצֵחַ שֶׁגָּלָה לָעִיר מִקְלָטוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic: honor given to a killer in the city of refuge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A killer offered honor in his city of refuge must declare 'I am a killer'. If they insist, he may accept, learned from 'וזה דבר הרוצח'.
